subject: physical-education
title: Investigation or close reading: what the heart and lungs do during activity
focus: what the heart and lungs do during activity
essentialQuestion: What does activity do for my body, and how do I judge my own effort?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: The heart pumps blood; the lungs add oxygen to it.
During activity both work harder, so breathing and heartbeat speed up.
That change is the body doing its job, not a problem.
Regular activity makes the heart stronger over time.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Believing that being out of breath means something is wrong. Fix: explain it as a normal, temporary response that settles during cool-down.
keyPoints: The heart pumps blood; the lungs add oxygen to it.
During activity both work harder, so breathing and heartbeat speed up.
That change is the body doing its job, not a problem.
Regular activity makes the heart stronger over time.
privacySafeScenario: Assemble a personal activity circuit you enjoy, with an easier and a harder option for each station, and explain how you judge your own effort.
studentTask: The learner practises what the heart and lungs do during activity at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with what the heart and lungs do during activity and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about what the heart and lungs do during activity at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for what the heart and lungs do during activity.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Every fitness activity has a lower-impact, seated, and shorter-duration version. Intensity is chosen by the learner using their own sense of effort. No learner is timed against another, ranked, or measured; there is no fitness test, no score, and no body measurement.
extensionChallenge: Apply what the heart and lungs do during activity under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises what the heart and lungs do during activity. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
